proposal.summary: Incorrect size checks when parsing IOAccelKernelCommand in IOAccelCommandQueue2::processSegmentKernelCommand() omit the 8-byte IOAccelKernelCommand header, allowing up to 8 bytes of out-of-bounds parsing. Command type 2 (kIOAccelKernelCommandCollectTimeStamp) performs a write into that out-of-bounds memory in shared memory, enabling overwrite of the first 1-8 bytes of the subsequent page. A PoC triggers the issue on iOS 13 (iPod9,1 build 17B111).
proposal.affected_product: iOS 13 (tested on iPod9,1 build 17B111); macOS: unknown

proposal.recommended_next_step: Reproduce the issue using the provided PoC on the reported build(s) and confirm the out-of-bounds write, then fix IOAccelCommandQueue2::processSegmentKernelCommand() to include the 8-byte header in size checks and audit AGXCommandQueue parsing for similar shared-memory double-fetch and non-volatile access issues.

evidence_quotes.claim: Size check excludes header causing OOB parsing
evidence_quotes.quote: the check excludes the size of the 8-byte header, meaning that processSegmentKernelCommand() will parse up to 8 bytes of out-of-bounds data.
The IOAccelKernelCommand is being parsed from shared memory, so the write is visible to userspace.

evidence_quotes.claim: Command type 2 writes into OOB memory
evidence_quotes.quote: However, command type 2 corresponds to kIOAccelKernelCommandCollectTimeStamp, which actually *writes* into the OOB memory rather than just parsing data from it.
This makes it possible to overwrite the first 1-8 bytes of the subsequent page of memory with timestamp data.
The attached POC should trigger the issue on iOS 13. Tested on iPod9,1 17B111.
